title: Queue backlog that never drains
description: An analytics service writes click events to one PostgreSQL primary, which commits about 8k inserts/s. Traffic grew to a steady 15k events/s, so the team put Kafka in front of the database. Kafka consumer lag now grows every hour and never recovers. Which change actually fixes the problem?

options.text: Add Redis in front of PostgreSQL to cache recent events.
options.explanation: Caching helps reads. Every event still has to be persisted, so a cache does not raise write throughput.

options.text: Add more Kafka partitions and consumers but keep writing one row per event to the same primary.
options.explanation: More consumers only push harder on the same 8k/s ceiling; the database is the bottleneck.

options.text: Add two read replicas so the primary has more capacity for writes.
options.explanation: Replicas take reads off the primary, but this workload is insert-bound, and replication adds work for every write.

options.text: Batch inserts in the consumers and partition the table across several database nodes by a high-cardinality key such as event source ID.
options.explanation: The sustained arrival rate exceeds commit capacity. Batching cuts per-row overhead and sharding adds parallel write capacity; the queue keeps absorbing bursts while capacity catches up.
